def match(pattern: str, text: str) -> bool:
    """
    Implements a regular expression matching algorithm supporting
    literal characters, '.', '*' (zero or more of the preceding 
    element), and '+' (one or more of the preceding element) 
    using recursion with memoization for efficient matching.
    """

    memo = {}

    def is_match(p_idx: int, t_idx: int) -> bool:
        if (p_idx, t_idx) in memo:
            return memo[(p_idx, t_idx)]

        if p_idx == len(pattern) and t_idx == len(text):
            return True

        # Handling '*' operator
        if p_idx + 1 < len(pattern) and pattern[p_idx + 1] == '*':
            result = (is_match(p_idx + 2, t_idx) or   # Match zero occurrence
                      (t_idx < len(text) and (pattern[p_idx] == text[t_idx] or pattern[p_idx] == '.') and 
                       is_match(p_idx, t_idx + 1)))  # Match one or more occurrences
            memo[(p_idx, t_idx)] = result
            return result

        # Handling '+' operator
        if p_idx + 1 < len(pattern) and pattern[p_idx + 1] == '+':
            result = (t_idx < len(text) and (pattern[p_idx] == text[t_idx] or pattern[p_idx] == '.') and 
                      (is_match(p_idx, t_idx + 1) or 
                       (t_idx + 1 < len(text) and is_match(p_idx + 2, t_idx + 1)))) 
            )
            memo[(p_idx, t_idx)] = result
            return result

        # Regular character and '.' matching
        if p_idx < len(pattern) and t_idx < len(text) and (pattern[p_idx] == text[t_idx] or pattern[p_idx] == '.'):
            result = is_match(p_idx + 1, t_idx + 1)
            memo[(p_idx, t_idx)] = result
            return result

        memo[(p_idx, t_idx)] = False
        return False

    return is_match(0, 0)
